t: For necessary expenses of the Financial Management Service, $184,300,000, of which not to exceed $14,277,000 shall remain available until expended for systems modernization initiatives. In addition, $90,000, to be derived from the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund, to reimburse the Service for administrative and personnel expenses for financial management of the Fund, as authorized by section 1012 of Public Law 101–380.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision funding the Financial Management Service and reimbursing it from the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision; there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. The only possible temptation is the reference to a trust fund or 'financial management', but that is an internal federal accounting matter.
fable.s: For necessary expenses of the Financial Management Service, $184,300,000, of which not to exceed $14,277,000 shall remain available until expended for systems modernization initiatives.

opus.w: This section only sets funding amounts for the Financial Management Service and arranges a reimbursement from the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund. It calls for no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved. The citation of authorizing law is boilerplate and creates no outside-party process.
opus.s: For necessary expenses of the Financial Management Service, $184,300,000, of which not to exceed $14,277,000 shall remain available until expended for systems modernization initiatives.
opus.b: This is a pure appropriations provision, so the answer is No. The tempting misreading is that "authorized by section 1012 of Public Law 101–380" brings in an outside process. It doesn't: the reference is only the legal authority for a reimbursement. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.
